source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 13–16, Assumption 5.11, Theorem 5.14, and Design A discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 5.14 obtains a realized-QV studentized fixed-horizon normal pivot without deterministic variance stabilization; the paper explicitly says it accommodates random limits and illustrates two post-burn-in variance regimes.

The paper's IPW score has conditional mean equal to its population moment and, under scaled inverse-propensity convergence, gives deterministic Gaussian IPW-Z limits with a consistent asymptotic-variance estimator.
Directional stability is presented as weaker than target-agnostic/full-matrix stability and yields asymptotic normality and efficiency for scalar targets.
The paper targets a projected parameter under a fixed evaluation policy and obtains inference under persistent, potentially nonconvergent logging by estimating time-varying score variance.

For generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, the optimal-arm pull/noise process has a unique SDE invariant law, while normalized arm means are Gaussian in stable cases and have a non-Gaussian limit in unstable optimal-arm cases.

The article gives a lower bound on convergence to a prescribed point conditional on being in its domain of attraction for a stochastic-approximation recursion with finitely many possible limit points.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, asymptotic regime discussion; pp. 23 and 32–33, adaptive sandwich variance
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses growing numbers of users with a fixed number of decision times and develops an adaptive sandwich variance estimator for that pooled longitudinal regime.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the slope-only “Markov recursion on K_GX” handle with an augmented state containing both ridge Gram and response states, then prove or explicitly require a compact invariant/absorbing set before applying ODE methods.

Derive the attraction modulus for one named clipped adaptive policy on a nontrivial basin-interior regime; this would turn the main result from a bespoke conditional uniformization into a practically checkable theorem.
Move the single-attractor reduction into a sanity-reduction paragraph and add a quantitative finite-T coverage/error bound for the realized-QV pivot in terms of r_T and delta_T.

recommended_next_step: Revise the Guo--Xu dynamics question with a genuine Markov state and remove the vacuous single-attractor proposition; retain the main bundle explicitly as a conditional field-tier result.
